page: Amazon Web Services m6in.12xlarge is an x86_64 general purpose cloud server built on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. The instance is powered by a dedicated 24-core Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz, supplying 48 virtual CPUs via two threads per physical core. System memory totals 192 GB of DDR4 running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. Cache configuration comprises 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 54 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by instruction sets such as AVX-512, SHA, and AES extensions.

The hardware configuration does not include local disk storage, requiring storage allocation via remote Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) attachments. It contains no dedicated GPU hardware accelerators. To handle network-dense workloads, the instance is engineered with a high baseline network bandwidth of 75 Gbps, making it structurally distinct from standard general purpose types that operate with lower network interfaces.

Benchmark measurements place the instance in the middle 50% for standard multi-core processing, single-core execution, and RAM access metrics. It registered 45.59 million operations per second on Redis SET tests and 41.66 GB/sec in static web throughput. Relative strengths appear in PassMark CPU encryption benchmarks as well as Geekbench ray tracing and image processing, where it ranks in the top 25%. Qualitatively, the instance balances extensive core density and memory with exceptional network throughput, presenting a viable hardware profile for distributed caching tiers, network-intensive container clusters, data extraction pipelines, and microservice backends.
description: Amazon Web Services m6in.12xlarge is an x86_64 general purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and equipped with an Intel Xeon 8375C processor operating at 3.5 GHz. The configuration features 48 dedicated vCPUs, 24 physical cores, and 192 GB of DDR4 system memory, reflecting a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM allocation. The server includes no bundled local disks or GPU accelerators, relying on external block storage architectures. A prominent attribute is its 75 Gbps baseline network throughput. Performance testing indicates average tiers across general compute, web serving (41.66 GB/sec), and Redis caching operations (45.59 million operations/sec), with top-quartile results in hardware encryption, image processing, and ray tracing. The instance matches requirements for network-constrained enterprise applications, distributed databases, large-scale web services, and ETL pipelines.
